pr.title: Fix #124478 - offset_of! returns a temporary
pr.description:
This was due to the must_use() call. Adding HIR's `OffsetOf` to the must_use checking within the compiler avoids this issue while maintaining the lint output.

Fixes #124478. @tgross35
pr.author: GKFX

issues.title: `offset_of` returns a temporary
issues.body:
I tried this code:

```rust
struct Foo {
    a: u32,
}

impl Foo {
    fn bar() -> &'static [usize] {
        &[std::mem::offset_of!(Self, a)]
    }
}
```

[Playground link](https://play.rust-lang.org/?version=nightly&mode=debug&edition=2021&gist=91f57feb9b8919f9fb5f115a272ea6da)

I expected to see this happen: no error

Instead, this happened:

```text
error[E0515]: cannot return reference to temporary value
 --> src/lib.rs:7:9
  |
7 |         &[std::mem::offset_of!(Self, a)]
  |         ^-------------------------------
  |         ||
  |         |temporary value created here
  |         returns a reference to data owned by the current function

For more information about this error, try `rustc --explain E0515`.
error: could not compile `playground` (lib) due to 1 previous error
```

processing.reason: The historical regression is a compile-time lifetime/promotion bug, not a runtime miscompilation with different values. The pre-fix expansion `crate::hint::must_use({builtin # offset_of(...)})` and the fixed expansion `{builtin # offset_of(...)}` both evaluate to exactly the same `usize` offset; `must_use` is an identity wrapper. The historical failure is that the wrapper creates a function-call temporary, so `&[offset_of!(Self, v), ...]` cannot be returned as `&'static [usize]` and rustc emits E0515. A source-grounded pair would therefore have to either (a) differ only by the identity `must_use` wrapper—producing identical values while passing Miri—or (b) model the rejected borrow by returning a dangling/temporary reference, which cannot pass Miri. Producing different numeric values would require an arbitrary semantic change to `must_use` or the offset expression, which would not be the historical transformation. Thus no valid pair can satisfy both the both-pass-Miri and different-values requirements.

analysis.summary: Confirmed bug fix for #124478: the `offset_of!` macro wrapped the `builtin # offset_of(...)` rvalue in `crate::hint::must_use(...)`, which made the result a function-call temporary and broke static promotion/borrowing (`&[offset_of!(Self, a)]` could not be returned as `&'static [usize]`). The fix removes the `must_use` wrapper from the macro and instead teaches the compiler's unused-results lint to recognize HIR `ExprKind::OffsetOf` as must-use. In MIR, both DataflowConstProp and GVN can fold the `OffsetOf` rvalue directly to a constant once there is no intervening `must_use` call. This is a confirmed bug fix, not an optimization PR; no compiler was built and no execution is claimed.
analysis.originalLogic: The core `offset_of!` macro expanded to `crate::hint::must_use({builtin # offset_of($Container, $($fields)+)})`, with `#[allow_internal_unstable(builtin_syntax, hint_must_use)]`. Thus the builtin `OffsetOf` rvalue was passed through a `must_use` function call. In MIR this appeared as, for example, `_2 = OffsetOf(Alpha, [(0, 0)]); _1 = must_use::<usize>(move _2) -> [return: bb1, unwind ...];`, and after const propagation as `_2 = const 4_usize; _1 = must_use::<usize>(const 4_usize) -> ...`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect transformation was wrapping the `offset_of` builtin rvalue in `crate::hint::must_use(...)`. This turned the offset value into a function-call temporary instead of allowing the `OffsetOf` rvalue to be directly materialized/const-promoted. Consequently a reference such as `&[offset_of!(Self, a)]` borrowed a temporary and failed with `error[E0515]: cannot return reference to temporary value`. The corrected form returns the builtin directly, `{builtin # offset_of($Container, $($fields)+)}`, and preserves the must-use behavior by adding `hir::ExprKind::OffsetOf(..) => Some(\"`offset_of` call\")` in the lint, so MIR can fold the `OffsetOf` directly to a constant.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust source using `core::mem::offset_of!`/`std::mem::offset_of!` as a value where its result must be const-promoted or borrowed with a `'static` lifetime, e.g. returning `&'static [usize]` from `&[offset_of!(Self, v), offset_of!(Self, w)]`, taking `let r = &offset_of!(Self, v);`, or otherwise relying on the offset expression not creating a temporary. Also covers the unused-result lint domain: a bare `offset_of!(...)` statement should still warn.
analysis.trigger: The bug triggers when `offset_of!` is expanded through the `must_use()` wrapper and then used in a reference/const-promotion context, especially returning a reference to an array/slice literal containing an `offset_of!` element from a function whose return type requires `'static` data.
preconditions: The pre-fix `offset_of!` macro body calls `crate::hint::must_use(...)` around the builtin offset expression.
The offset expression is used as a value that must be promoted to a static/const (e.g. an element of a returned `&'static [usize]`).
For the lint half, the compiler's unused-results lint must be updated to classify `hir::ExprKind::OffsetOf` as producing a must-use value so removing `must_use` does not regress the warning.
pitfalls: Do not add a function-call wrapper (such as `must_use`) around the `OffsetOf` rvalue: it creates a temporary and blocks static promotion, causing E0515 in reference-returning contexts.
When removing the `must_use` wrapper, the unused-result lint must still fire; dropping the wrapper without adding HIR `OffsetOf` handling silently loses `unused_must_use` coverage.
The lint message changes from `unused return value of `must_use` that must be used` to `unused `offset_of` call that must be used`, so tests expecting the old message must be updated.

Do not mistake the MIR expectation changes for a new incorrect pass rewrite: DataflowConstProp and GVN are correctly folding `OffsetOf` to a constant; the removed `must_use::<usize>(...)` call is what previously blocked direct promotion.
Outer test-expectation edits and line-number shifts in stderr files are consequences of removing the call, not separate semantic changes.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a build-pass UI regression test using `offset_of!` in const-promotion/reference contexts: `fn return_static_slice() -> &'static [usize] { &[offset_of!(Self, v), offset_of!(Self, w)] }` and `fn use_reference() -> usize { let r = &offset_of!(Self, v); *r * 6 }`. Keep a UI lint test that uses bare `offset_of!` as a statement and expects the warning `unused `offset_of` call that must be used` with the annotation `the `offset_of` call produces a value`. In MIR-opt tests, check that concrete offsets directly become `_1 = const 4_usize` (no `must_use::<usize>` call) and generic offsets remain `OffsetOf(Gamma<T>, ...)` until instantiated; verify both GVN and DataflowConstProp diffs.
